Find the area $A$ between the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{x+8}-2$, the $y$-axis and the lines $y=-2$ and $y=0,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$

{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{x+8}-2 \\ y+2 & =\sqrt[3]{x+8} \\ (y+2)^{3} & =x+8 \\ x & =(y+2)^{3}-8 \\ x & ={y}^{3}+6{y}^{2}+12y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}({y}^{3}+6{y}^{2}+12y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{-2}^{0}\,+\,6\cdot {\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{-2}^{0}+12\cdot {\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =(0-\frac{16}{4})+6(0-(-\frac{8}{3}))+12(0-\frac{4}{2}) \\  & =-4+16-24 \\  & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

We obtained a negative number because the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis. So the area that we want is

$$
A=|-12|=12\,.
$$
